scope: Twelve excerpt-level claim interpretation cases. Four published historical antibody-engineering papers. No new protein designs or de novo competition eligibility claims.

sources.title: A stepwise mutagenesis approach using histidine and acidic amino acid to engineer highly pH-dependent protein switches
sources.source_text: Nine pH-dependent antibodies were isolated using single-acidic amino acid residue mutagenesis at the six hot-spot residue positions.
sources.reuse_note: Only a short attributed excerpt (at most 25 words) is redistributed; no full text is bundled. Check the original rights for further reuse.

sources.title: Structure-based engineering of pH-dependent antibody binding for selective targeting of solid-tumor microenvironment
sources.source_text: Binding selectivity toward acidic pH was improved by as much as 25-fold relative to the parental bH1-Fab.
sources.reuse_note: Only a short attributed excerpt (at most 25 words) is redistributed; no full text is bundled. Check the original rights for further reuse.

sources.title: Construction of pH-sensitive Her2-binding IgG1-Fc by directed evolution
sources.source_text: Interestingly, two of the three Fcabs did not contain a single histidine mutation
sources.reuse_note: Only a short attributed excerpt (at most 25 words) is redistributed; no full text is bundled. Check the original rights for further reuse.

sources.title: A generic approach to engineer antibody pH-switches using combinatorial histidine scanning libraries and yeast display
sources.source_text: The strategy allows simultaneous screening for both, high affinity binding at pH 7.4 and pH-sensitivity, and excludes conventional negative selection steps.
sources.reuse_note: Only a short attributed excerpt (at most 25 words) is redistributed; no full text is bundled. Check the original rights for further reuse.

cases.claim: The excerpt reports nine pH-dependent antibodies obtained through acidic-residue mutagenesis.
cases.draft_rationale: The passage states nine antibodies and describes the mutagenesis approach.

cases.claim: The excerpt reports only one pH-dependent antibody obtained through that mutagenesis.
cases.draft_rationale: The passage specifies nine rather than one.

cases.claim: These nine antibodies were shown to improve survival in a randomized human trial.
cases.draft_rationale: The supplied excerpt has no clinical trial or survival evidence.

cases.claim: The excerpt reports up to a 25-fold improvement in acidic-pH binding selectivity over parental bH1-Fab.
cases.draft_rationale: The reported direction, maximum magnitude and comparator match.

cases.claim: The excerpt reports up to a 25-fold reduction in acidic-pH binding selectivity over parental bH1-Fab.
cases.draft_rationale: The passage reports improvement rather than reduction.

cases.claim: The excerpt establishes that the same designs bind both human and mouse EGFR.
cases.draft_rationale: The excerpt provides neither EGFR cross-species results nor those measurements.

cases.claim: The excerpt states that two of three Fcabs had no histidine mutation.
cases.draft_rationale: This is the scoped observation directly reported in the passage.

cases.claim: The excerpt states that all three Fcabs contained a histidine mutation.
cases.draft_rationale: Two of three are explicitly reported without such a mutation.

cases.claim: The excerpt gives an exact dissociation constant of 1 nanomolar for these Fcabs.
cases.draft_rationale: The passage contains no dissociation constant.

cases.claim: The excerpt describes screening at pH 7.4 without conventional negative selection steps.
cases.draft_rationale: Both the pH condition and exclusion of negative selection are stated.

cases.claim: The excerpt says conventional negative selection steps are required by this strategy.
cases.draft_rationale: The passage explicitly says conventional negative selection steps are excluded.

cases.claim: This screening strategy guarantees therapeutic efficacy in all tumor types.
cases.draft_rationale: The provided passage gives no universal therapeutic efficacy evidence.
